name: scenario-to-desktop.pipeline-inspect
purpose: Inspect one desktop pipeline and its investigation tasks without restarting work or treating packaging success as release approval.

pipeline_id.description: Exact pipeline ID; empty selects the newest created pipeline for the scenario.

assumptions: The caller uses the declared scenario bindings and preserves unavailable evidence.
Program success describes the read; it never grants deployment approval.
invariants: The envelope is printed exactly once on every path.
Read-only: no launch, build, publication, recovery, inference, delegation, or memory write.
Return identifiers and bounded projections; never print logs, configuration, credentials, media bytes, or private endpoints.
An explicit pipeline ID must match the requested scenario.
At most ten stages and five task references cross the envelope.

signals.pipeline: Exact identity, owner status, current stage, error-presence flags, and at most ten stage summaries; null if unreadable.
signals.task_count: Observed task count, capped at 100; null when the task read failed.
signals.task_states: Owner status distribution within the bounded task sample; unknown remains unknown.
signals.tasks: At most five task ID/status references.
signals.tasks_truncated: True when more tasks exist than returned.
signals.task_sample_saturated: True at 100 returned tasks; additional server-side tasks may exist.

outputs.evidence: Successfully read binding IDs; selected pipeline or capture identities are in signals.

fixtures.note: Read-only. Requires at least one existing hello-desktop pipeline. Discovers the ID at fixture time; owner pipeline failure is diagnostic data, not a failed read.
